stemMd: In a triangle, sides of lengths 5 and 7 enclose an angle of 60°. What is the length of the opposite side?
explanationMd: The cosine rule gives c²=5²+7²−2×5×7×cos60°. Since cos60°=1/2, this is 25+49−35=39, so c=√39. The included angle, rather than a right angle, determines the correction term.

distractorRationale.a: This omits the cosine-law subtraction term.
distractorRationale.e: This assumes the sides point in the same direction.
distractorRationale.d: This adds the two sides, which would require a degenerate triangle.
distractorRationale.b: This does not satisfy the cosine-law calculation.
